what: The rules by which several judgings of one cell's attempts compose into the cell's served figure, as the package's land.pooling module implements them. The entries are copied from the project's rule file (the consumer-contract side of its split, with the consumed rules its archive parts hold) under plain names, each with its source key, the source file's sha16 and the date of the decision; within an entry everything but the provenance (who decided, when, the witnesses and the counts) travels. The texts are the source's sentences with role words in place of the team names the publication does not carry (the role words are listed under substitutions), stamps of provenance dropped, and a prose quotation replaced by a marker; a key named candidate carries a rule not yet decided. An entry marked restated would carry a sentence written for this copy; none does.

source.file: the project's winner rule, consumer-contract side, with its two archive parts
source.split: only keys loaders read; the record file beside it is not published

substitutions_note: each role word above stands where the source names a part of the project's team, its machines or its working trees; the source's own names are not reproduced
walk_key: grade (the applicable corrections the stamp carries)
not more lenient than the current comparison or cap
the task-scoped currencies (the leading-imports rule's version, the plus filter) on listed tasks
walk_key_note: The survivor-passes term of the collector's overlay walk ranks continuation emissions among same-rank rows only and never decides which judging row wins a draw; among equal ranks the later emission wins, so a later re-emission of the same rank never lowers a served figure.

rule.identity_correction: contradictions are evaluated WITHIN a draw (hashed rows by task_samples_sha256; unhashed rows join only a single-draw cell); a key whose zero and non-zero instants belong to DIFFERENT draws (regenerated or dual-generation legs on one shard) is 'different-draws' — no contradiction, no hold, no window; each draw stands on its rows and the two pool. The scan's window exclusion is per-task, so every key with a zero and a higher-tier non-zero on the same draw has an explicit status.

identity_stands_under_a_re_layout_by_rou.rule: a row's identity of record is task_samples_sha256 by the recipe of record (the identity recipe; the RULES of 2 Sep 16:05 UTC): the sha256 over the SORTED 'solution' strings of the task's own rows in the judged samples file as written - no shard name, no file name, no route and no override enters it - so a RE-LAYOUT that copies rows byte for byte into shards of another name and route keeps every task's identity unchanged; the file-level samples_sha256 is the new file's and binds nothing (a hash computed any other way than the recipe binds to nothing); the census cell key (configuration, task) is unchanged; the draw key (shard, source, identity) carries the new shard name, and because the half left under the old name is judged on an override trimmed to its own rows, one identity is never judged under two shard names - no second draw, no twin-label pair, nothing voided (nothing of these shards served before the re-layout)
identity_stands_under_a_re_layout_by_rou.scope: the Mbpp-form shards of every checkpoint read of the series r1d7b-rl-f12-a-step<NNNN>_think_temp_0.6 (14 of 45 per checkpoint and their _d continuations): the plain Mbpp rows (numeric ids) re-laid under <shard>m/mbpp/ with an override of those rows alone, judged under the mbpp route with the start model's own stamp token for token; the twins and the non-Mbpp rows staying under <shard>/humaneval/ with the override trimmed to them; the same form for any later re-layout by route
identity_stands_under_a_re_layout_by_rou.what_the_store_reads: the two halves' cells as ONE configuration's (the census cell is keyed by configuration and task; a task appears in one half only); the per-checkpoint declared landing lists re-cut to carry both halves of every Mbpp-form shard (the m shard and its m_d continuation beside the humaneval half and its _d) from the training reads' owner manifest of the halves, before the first re-laid cells land; the rows judged under the mbpp route carry the mbpp route's ruled knobs (compare=numeric-tolerant-v2, stdout_compare=v2-symmetric-r2), current under the per-route rule as the start model's wave1_mbpp rows are
identity_stands_under_a_re_layout_by_rou.not_a_new_era: no judge code changes, no stamp is new, no correction era: the comparator route per row class is the route the start model's rows of that class were judged under

clock_boundary_2026-09-06.class: JUDGE-CLOCK-BOUNDARY: an attempt whose runtime sits at a per-input limit (15 s floor or 4 × canonical) or at the whole-task cap passes or fails with node load — the verdict is a property of the node, not of the program
clock_boundary_2026-09-06.store_rule: within one stamp era, an attempt whose identical text (solution_sha256) has both a valid PASS and a valid FAIL judging under identical knobs and reference is SERVED AS PASS with a receipt (a deterministic program that passed once is correct and within the limit; the fail is environmental — evalplus' per-input time-out reads as a plain fail, so the flip itself is the witness); implemented as an attempt-level overlay (the continuation overlay's path) written by the judge with receipts (attempt, the two judgings' ts/hosts, knobs), consumed by the fold, the certificate builder and the pool pages; the cell carries a flag count clock_boundary_restores; no third status; nondeterministic programs (random/time/order-dependent) are the one exception and are named per receipt when found

hashless_attribution_key.rule: a hashless judging row binds to the identity mirror's generation event under the FULL key (config, shard, task, generation_host, leg_source): generation_host and leg_source come from the ROW's own run_dir (the second cluster's when the run_dir is under the second cluster's work tree or a the carried-copy tree tree — carry copies are the second cluster's legs byte for byte; box for boxjudge; else the first cluster's), and the mirror line's from its samples_path (/the carried-copy tree/ → the carried-copy tree, else runs). A label (config, shard, task) carrying two hashes split across (the first cluster's, runs) and (the second cluster's, the carried-copy tree) is NOT ambiguous: it is the same shard generated on both clusters = two distinct draws, each judged, both pool. AMBIGUOUS (unpooled, flagged 'unattributed judging') = two or more hashes under the FULL key (idmirror_ambiguous), a two-hash label whose row host+source has no mirror entry, a boxjudge or non-project run_dir on a two-hash label, or a bound entry whose n_samples differs from the row's n_attempts.

hashed_rows_identity.rule: for a judging row that CARRIES task_samples_sha256, the row's own hash IS the draw identity of record — it is the pinned recipe computed by the fragment maker over the very samples file the judging read. The identity mirror is the identity SOURCE for rows born without a hash and a cross-check for hashed ones; it is never a precondition. A second hash under one shard is a second draw by definition (same-shard pooling: distinct draws pool), whether or not the mirror has been backfilled to carry it. So valid_cells' reading is the §1b reading: the certificate builder drops the mirror guard for hashed rows; the guard stays for hashless rows (hashless_attribution_key).
hashed_rows_identity.why_sound: two judgings of the SAME samples file under the same extractor produce the SAME hash (sanitization is deterministic) and compete within one draw (later ts wins); a hash can differ on one shard only when the samples differ (a second generation — e.g. the shard generated on both clusters, or a carry leg beside a box-judged local leg) or when the sanitizer/extractor changed — and extractor/sanitizer changes are ruled to be emitted as ALIAS rows binding through source_samples_sha256 (version_change_rule; reader_rule_overlays_and_aliases), never as plain re-judgings. That writer rule, not the mirror, is what excludes double counting.

redraw_overlay_composes_empty_or_cut_slo.rule: A redraw overlay row composes into the served row PER SLOT, and only into slots whose served answer is EMPTY (the empty-answer flag) or CUT (the truncation flag): there the redraw's completed reply supersedes the non-answer, as a continued draw supersedes its cut prefix - the ruled remedy, kept. A redraw of a slot that holds a delivered non-empty answer is OUT OF SCOPE: it does not compose; the served verdict of that slot stands; the redraw row remains a row of the same raw draw for the walk (one generation = one draw; a re-emitted subset is a re-judging or a redraw, never a continuation), and as a partial row it never serves over the complete row. The composed block records k_accepted (empty or cut slots) and k_rejected (out-of-scope slots) with their indices; cut_before is read from the SERVED row's own flags (empty + truncated among the overlay's indices), never from the overlay's claim.

unit_of_whole_2026-10-08.rule: THE UNIT OF 'WHOLE' IS THE LEG (the continued parent: every continued row of the leg under one judging), never a chunk. (1) A version WHOLE ON THE LEG composes by the ordinary time rule at the census it lands - a whole-leg re-judge landed by one block is such a version, whatever else is in flight on the same parent. (2) A version landing PIECEWISE (chunk rows whose union is not yet whole on the leg) never serves until its union is whole - not even a chunk that is itself whole. (3) While a piecewise version lands, the cell serves the NEWEST VERSION WHOLE ON THE LEG: the bound census's version by construction, or a whole version landed since the bound census if one exists; disclosed held_last_good only where the cell's served version is the bound census's and newer rows are set aside. (4) When the piecewise version's union is whole, the ordinary time rule applies again (the newest whole version wins).
unit_of_whole_2026-10-08.collector_form: the collector' v4v19i as derived (the lookup on the bound census's kept copy for the cells the lane gate HOLDS) yields this: a held cell takes the bound version; a cell whose new rows are a whole version is not held and composes them. The fold header names, per cell restored or set aside, which rule it took: 'whole version landed' (the ordinary rule) or 'held_last_good from the bound census <stamp>' (a piecewise landing in flight).
unit_of_whole_2026-10-08.why: the rule exists to keep a PARTIAL state off the served faces; a whole newer judging is not a partial state, and holding it for hours on the timing of a different landing of the same parent would make the cell's figure depend on a queue rather than on the rows. rule.clause: The served census pools every distinct draw of a task into its cell whatever the draws' judge stamps — the pool's identity is the draw's (shard, source, task_samples_sha256), each draw serving under its own judging of record; the extractor rule of 6 Sep governs within a draw (an x2 judging outranks a v1 judging of the same draw, never a bridge for restores) and says nothing against pooling distinct draws judged under different extractors. A cell pooling draws under more than one judge stamp is served and MARKED (the judge stamps pooled; the x2-judged share of its attempts), never held. The mixed state is a mixture of judge STAMPS: the extraction step's x2 emission writes an alias leg only where the corrected extractor changes at least one attempt's judged program, and an unchanged leg keeps its plain verdicts as the verdicts of record by design, so a plain-judged draw in a mixed cell carries verdicts the corrected extractor would not change; the mixed count does not fall on its own and is not a defect to retire — the mark is the truth of the state, and a gap between an x2-judged draw and a plain-judged draw of one task is a difference between draws, read per cell. The extractor dimension of a stamp is the same across the mix by the emission's design; the comparison-rule dimension (the compare and stdout_compare forms) is open to the check of record — the mixed cells' plain draws re-judged under the x2 legs' full stamp against their x2 draws (the judge, from the extraction step's reach record): verdicts that rise name the comparison era as the cause and open a scoped re-judge frame by set, verdicts that stay name a difference in the draws' generation (a shard and its re-draw under different templates or samplers), which the generation records read and the era lane carries as its own cells. The deep read's one-judge rule (the fit methods owner' (aaa)(h)(ii): a cell counted under the judge of its start draw of record) is the training read's own paired comparison, not the census's rule.

rule.clause: An x2 (alias) row binds to its draw ONLY through source_samples_sha256 equal to a v1 row's task_samples_sha256 as the identity recipe computes it (or the identity mirror's value for that draw, the recipe over the judged samples file) — never by task and shard, never by position, never on the x2 row's own hash standing as the draw's identity (a hash computed any other way binds to nothing; a derived row never asserts its own identity). A plain row that carries no task_samples_sha256 contributes no identity, so an x2 row for it is an ORPHAN — excluded from composition, counted on the header, never pooled as a new draw — and stays one after the cell composes until the plain row carries the hash, from its writer (the judge consumer writing task_samples_sha256 on every chunk-judged row, the landed rows backfilled from the legs' samples files by the recipe) or from the identity mirror's backfill over those legs; then the x2 row binds at the next fold and the cell moves from the plain to the x2 judging at equal n — a declared move under the configuration's x2 legs list, the orphan count falling, old and new to the owners. An x2 row judged before its plain row has landed is the orphan class's transient, binding when the plain row lands with its hash. The historical 'defect for extraction or the certificate builder' wording names only the third cause, a source hash that matches a landed, hashed plain row of nothing (a wrong hash) — the orphan block's text to name all three causes at the collector's next cut.

task_samples_sha256, the draw identity of record for every arm (the store's RULES of 2 Sep 2026 and the project's IDENTITY-RECIPE), is the recipe over the 'solution' strings of every row of the task in the judged samples file AS WRITTEN by the extractor — the file evalplus reads (<stem>.jsonl; the sanitized solutions, never the raw completion) — and never over strings a judging modifies at judging time: a judge knob that prepends an imports preamble, applies a typing fix or otherwise edits the strings it executes is an ERA of the judging, not a change of the draw, and the row it writes carries the identity of the written file (the consumer's typing-fix note of 1405: identity from --samples-full, the as-written file). So one draw keeps one identity across every judging era and every extractor pass of the same written file, and a derived row (an x2 alias, an overlay) binds through it; a judging whose row hashes the strings as modified can never bind the draw's alias rows and is a defect of the writer, fixed on the writer's side and backfilled as the written file's hash.

rule.rule: A judged row of a shard whose task_samples_sha256 matches neither the shard's CURRENT samples file nor a LIVE sibling placement of the same shard is a STALE-IDENTITY row of the same generation: its replies are the current file's replies under an earlier byte state of the file (a transient write, a sanitize pass, a re-derivation); it is SUPERSEDED by the current file's judging of the task and is never pooled as a distinct draw. The pool's identity rule of 3 Oct (shard, source, task_samples_sha256; one draw one identity across every judging and extractor pass of the same written file) stands for files whose bytes stood; where the bytes changed, the generation is one and the identity is the current file's. An @extractor-x2 alias row binds to the base file's identity (the collector resolves a re-extraction to the samples it re-extracts) and is governed within that draw by the extractor rule of 6 Sep.

rule.rule: Two generations of one shard name - the same shard generated on two clusters (each cluster's generation carried to the other), or a shard regenerated - are TWO DRAWS of the cell: distinct raw completions, distinct identities, pooled with n summed and each serving under its own judging of record (the 3 Sep tiebreak RULES's different-draws clause; the collector's reading since the Qwen3 think arms is the rule of record). A CARRIED COPY of a generation is the SAME draw as its source - the same raw, the same identity - and never pools with it (the twin-shard walk's collapse of same-raw placements). The per-route currency condition applies per DRAW: an old-judged generation is brought current by a re-judge of ITS legs (on the cluster where its generation is live, or its CARRIED COPY), never by dropping it. The stale-identity rule (stale_identity_rows_2026-10-05) keeps its text for an identity live in no file and has NO SUBJECT on the start model.

rule.rule: REPLACEMENT DRAW AT THE LIMIT OF RECORD: (1) a fresh placement of a cell under the same configuration id with a new shard name is a DRAW of the cell - its own identity by the recipe of record - never an overlay; nothing composes per sample. (2) Ordinarily a second generation POOLS with the first, n summed, each draw serving under its own judging of record (the 3 Sep tiebreak RULES's different-draws clause; the two-generations clause of 5 Oct) - pooling presumes both generations live in a file, each brought current by a re-judge of its own legs. (3) A draw whose raw completions are LIVE IN NO FILE - neither the shard's current samples file nor a live sibling placement carries its identity - can be neither re-judged, continued nor verified: it fails the per-draw currency condition for good, and under the project owner's word of about 13:20 local 7 Oct 2026 (every wave 1+2 read of record judged under the 4,096 limit) it can never be a read of record. Such a draw is RETIRED WHOLE - set aside from the pool and disclosed on the cell (retired_draws: shard, identity, kind 'source live in no file; re-drawn whole at the limit of record') - at the first census where a DECLARED REPLACEMENT draw of the cell at the limit of record has a valid judging, and not before: the cell serves its standing figures until the replacement composes (no placeholder between), then the replacement serves ALONE with its own n; the old and the new never pool. (4) The field is the store's DECLARED LIST of kind replacement-draw (knowledge/declared_legs/<list>.tsv: configuration_id, task, retired_shard, retired_identity, new_shard, limit, reason) - the collector reads the list and retires only what it names, by (configuration, task, retired shard) against the new shard once its judging is valid; a new_shard still PENDING retires nothing; a replacement nobody declared pools as any second generation would (the rule stays closed); the undeclared check credits the new shard's landing to the list. (5) No ts rank, no cap-era rank, no knob-era field decides it - a later-judging or newer-placement rule would retire every older draw of every cell that gains a placement. (6) A cell on the list leaves the continuation lists' expectation (its continuation cannot exist). (7) The stale-identity rule of 5 Oct is not the instrument: its subject is one generation under two byte states of ONE file, superseded by the current file's judging of the SAME task; where the shard's directory now holds another task's leg the clause has no subject, and the retirement is by this clause.

rule.the_stores_gate: after a whole re-judge of a served key's continued root under pins, the store holds that key's re-emission (the judge's refresh keeps the root excluded) until the judge's time-limit re-run of the audit's flips on the root has landed and judging has named the re-run's cells to the census readers; the store then says 'clear for re-emission: <key>' to the judge and the collector, the root re-emits, the served key moves once on verdicts of record at the next census, and the store's file of record on the key re-reads at its first bound census after the re-emission

rule.rule: TWO KINDS OF ROW WITHOUT A HASH. (a) A row born without task_samples_sha256 but judged on the WRITTEN file takes its identity by the one recipe over that file (the collector' identity_backfill; the identity mirror) and is a draw of record - the 4 Sep clause draw_identity_api_arms (the API arms' v1 rows, the older legs' rows; at census 579 the merge listing holds 356 such rows and 107 served cells rest on them, every one with the file's identity in the census). (b) A JUDGING WITHOUT IDENTITY is a judging whose rows carry no hash AND whose text was not the written file's - a torn or empty read (the judge's fragment finding: every row's solution sha empty; the audit's row-by-row read against the whole judgings; an evaluator's 'unknown' on every row): no identity by any recipe binds its verdicts to a draw, so it is no draw of record and binds to no draw on its own (stale_identity_rows_2026-10-05: a byte state that never stood). The census cannot tell (b) from (a) by its fields - the backfill gives both the file's identity - so the set of (b) is the judge's finding (its fragment list) and the store's test takes that list. FOR (b): where a judging WITH identity of the same (task, shard) exists, that judging is the record and the identity-less row is superseded whatever their timestamps (the collector's yield of an unhashed row to the hashed row of its own shard and file; the same-generation latest-ts rule never prefers an unhashed row; the partial-judging rule keeps a whole judging over a newer 8-row fragment). Where the identity-less row is the ONLY judging of a cell, the cell is UNRESOLVED IN IDENTITY: its served figure stands as the evaluator judged it until the judging with identity lands (the judge's re-judge of the task on the leg), the cell is named in the store's census read (state/scratch/identityless_served_<census>.json, from the judge's list) and in the record, and no file of record is cut with such a cell inside it (the per-attempt builder names the served draws whose listing row has no hash; a cell on the judge's list waits). From this clause's date a row of kind (b) entering ALONE does not compose a new cell (the collector's admission on the judge's list, the collector' implementation on this clause); no served cell is removed on this clause - the remedy is the judging with identity, never a hold that empties a cell, so nothing on a page moves by the clause itself.
rule.why: an identity-less row's verdicts may be the real text's (the audit's row-by-row read: 589 of 592 comparable rows equal to a whole judging of the same rows) or an evaluator's read of an empty file (eight 'fail unknown' rows where the whole judgings say wrong_answer on six); nothing in the row tells which, and the census's backfill gives the draw the file's identity so the census itself does not show the gap - only the listing's row does. A hashed judging of the same rows settles it; until then the cell is a verdict without a witness.
